title: Wedding catering checklist Dubai: confirm one complete plan
focus: Bring the menu, guest count, seating information and service timetable into a final brief that the couple, planner and catering contact can all use. Identify who approves changes and who coordinates with the venue. Include dietary meals, supplier meals and any late-evening food so they are not left to assumptions. The checklist should reflect the deadlines in the actual proposal. A clear handover before the wedding helps the team run the service while the couple enjoys the celebration.

sections.title: Connect the wedding meal with the celebration around it
paragraphs: The catering schedule should reflect the ceremony, photographs, speeches and the way guests will move through the venue. Decide when you want the first food served and whether the evening will progress from a reception into a seated meal or remain more informal.

A tasting can help you discuss flavour and presentation, but the final service also depends on quantities, equipment and staffing. Confirm how the chosen dishes will work for the complete guest count and how dietary alternatives will be served. If a cake is supplied separately, identify who receives, stores and presents it.

Give the catering team a current version of the programme and a contact for coordination. Changes to timing can affect the kitchen and service sequence, so keep updates in one clear channel. The aim is a meal that belongs naturally within the celebration and allows you to stay present with your guests.

sections.title: Build the service schedule around your guests
paragraphs: Work backwards from the time guests should begin eating. The team may need access earlier for unloading, setup and preparation, particularly when equipment or several service areas are involved. Share the programme before the menu is finalised so the catering plan can support it.

Identify moments when service should pause, such as a speech, presentation or ceremony. For an office event, confirm the length of each break and whether everyone will arrive at once. For a private celebration, allow for the welcome period and any cake or toast that needs its own place in the sequence.

Agree a contact for changes on the day. Small timing adjustments may be manageable, while a substantial extension can affect staffing and the booked hours. Clear communication helps the team respond sensibly and keeps the food connected to the occasion rather than running on a separate timetable.

sections.title: Give every guest a considered option
paragraphs: Collect dietary requirements before the final menu is agreed. Record how many guests each requirement applies to and distinguish preferences from allergies or other essential restrictions. A clear list helps the culinary team assess suitable dishes and the preparation arrangements they would need.

A vegetarian or vegan choice should feel like a complete part of the menu. Consider its portion, accompaniments and presentation alongside the other dishes, rather than removing an ingredient and assuming the result will be satisfying. Sauces, garnishes, breads and desserts also need attention.

Allergy requests require a specific discussion of ingredients and kitchen conditions. Labels and separate serving utensils can support a plan, but they do not by themselves guarantee the absence of cross-contact. Share the details early so the team can assess the request honestly and confirm what can be accommodated before you book.
